name: Potato Late Blight
symptoms: Water-soaked, pale green spots on leaves
White fungal growth on the underside of leaves in humid weather
prevention: Ensure proper plant spacing for air circulation
management: Apply protective fungicides before infection occurs
Remove and destroy infected plant debris

name: Potato Early Blight
symptoms: Small, dark spots on older leaves
Spots enlarge and form concentric rings (target board appearance)
Leaves turn yellow and drop prematurely
prevention: Maintain adequate plant nutrition and moisture
management: Apply appropriate fungicides at early symptom onset
Remove infected plant debris after harvest

name: Tomato Late Blight
symptoms: Irregular, dark, water-soaked patches on leaves
White mold on undersides of leaves in wet weather
Firm, dark brown spots on fruit
favorableConditions: Cloudy days with prolonged leaf wetness
prevention: Stake tomatoes to improve air circulation
management: Apply fungicides preventatively during favorable weather
Promptly remove and destroy infected plants

name: Tomato Target Spot
symptoms: Small brown lesions with light centers on leaves
Concentric rings may appear as spots enlarge
Brown lesions with sunken centers on fruit
favorableConditions: High humidity and prolonged leaf wetness
prevention: Ensure good air circulation through spacing and pruning
management: Use recommended fungicides if symptoms spread rapidly

name: Pepper Bacterial Spot
symptoms: Small, yellow-green spots on leaves turning brown/black
favorableConditions: High humidity and frequent rainfall or overhead irrigation
prevention: Avoid working in the field when plants are wet
management: Apply copper-based bactericides early in the season
